title: Shopping at the Supermarket
audience: Chinese primary school students (10-12 years old, average level in mainland China)
imageAlt: A girl shopping at a fruit supermarket with a list and 20 yuan, while a shopkeeper weighs an apple
imageDescription: A bright fruit corner in a supermarket. A big yellow price board on top reads APPLES 5, BANANAS 6, WATERMELON 12, each line with a picture of the fruit. Below the board, wooden shelves hold red apples, yellow bananas, and green watermelons, with oranges at the far right. On the left, a girl with short black hair, white shirt and green vest holds a shopping LIST that reads apple, banana, watermelon with small fruit pictures, and a 20 yuan banknote in her other hand. A thought bubble above her head shows an apple, bananas and a watermelon. In front of her is a red-handled shopping cart containing two apples, a bunch of bananas and one small watermelon. On the right, a smiling shopkeeper in an orange apron puts a red apple on an old-style balance scale to weigh it.
scoringDescription: A colorful cartoon supermarket fruit section. The key element is a large yellow price board with three lines in black text: APPLES 5 (with a red apple picture), BANANAS 6 (with a bunch of yellow bananas), WATERMELON 12 (with a green watermelon). For arithmetic questions, treat the prices as: apples 5 yuan per kilo, bananas 6 yuan per kilo, watermelon 12 yuan per piece. Below the board are wooden display shelves: red apples on the left, yellow bananas in the middle, round green watermelons on the right, and a pile of oranges at the far right edge. On the left stands a girl with short black hair, white long-sleeve shirt, green vest and dark blue skirt. In her right hand she holds a white paper LIST with three lines, each with a fruit picture and word: apple, banana, watermelon. In her left hand she holds up a green banknote printed with the number 20, meaning she has 20 yuan. A thought bubble above her head shows an apple, a bunch of bananas and a watermelon - the same three fruits she plans to buy. In front of her is a metal shopping cart with a red handle holding exactly two red apples, one bunch of yellow bananas and one small green watermelon. On the right, a young shopkeeper in a white shirt and orange apron smiles while placing a red apple on the pan of an old two-pan balance scale with a metal weight on the other side, weighing the apple for the customer. Expected math: one kilo of apples plus one kilo of bananas costs 5 + 6 = 11 yuan; after buying both from 20 yuan, 9 yuan is left; all three fruits cost 5 + 6 + 12 = 23 yuan, more than 20, so she cannot buy everything with 20 yuan. The cart already has fruit, while the thought bubble shows what she is thinking about buying.
